subject: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy

Alex — great conversation earlier. Thanks for walking us through the FinPay payment orchestration flow and the peak-week behavior. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we stay aligned on SLO qualification and quota asks: 

- Key targets you mentioned:
  - 99th pct latency target: 300ms for short responses (non-streaming), goal 95% under 150ms for interactive paths
  - Sustained throughput: ~850 requests/sec during business hours, peak spikes up to ~2,400 req/s for 90s bursts during batch settlement windows
  - Concurrent long-poll/streaming sessions: ~5k active customer streams; typical per-stream token throughput ~5-15 tokens/sec
  - Connection reuse policy: client pools will maintain ~500 TCP connections per region, with multiplexing at the app layer planned

- Open questions for engineering qualification (can you confirm the items below?):
  1) The 2,400 req/s spikes — are they single-second bursts or multi-minute windows? If multi-minute, what's the 95th/99th distribution window?
  2) For streaming sessions, are sessions sticky to a single connection/host or can they be migrated (you mentioned sticky session affinity today)?
  3) Are request payloads typically short (<1kB) or do you have large request bodies for enrichment?

Attached is a short note with Redwood SLO options and a proposed pilot quota matrix to discuss (redwood-slo-options.pdf).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Priya / Alex: share the traffic matrix export (CSV) so we can map to connection/streaming profiles.
- Redwood: we’ll propose an initial quota profile (baseline concurrency + burst windows + streaming token allowance) and a pilot timeline.
- Quick follow-up call Thurs or next Mon to lock pilot scope.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Lead, Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199
[Attachment: redwood-slo-options.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy

Thanks Marissa — this captures it well. Quick answers inline: 

- The 2.4k spikes are typically 60–120s windows during settlement cutovers (not single-second microbursts). We saw this pattern in last three monthly runs.
- Streaming sessions are sticky by design today (we bind sessions to a specific host/connection for KV cache locality). Migration is non-trivial and we prefer not to require it for the pilot.
- Payloads are small to medium: 70% <1kB, 25% 1–5kB (enrichment), 5% >5kB.

We’ll export the traffic matrix and Priya will share it by end of day.

Alex
VP Product, FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy

Appreciate the quick clarifications, Alex. A couple of follow-ups before we review the traffic matrix: 

- For the pilot quota proposal we’ll model two modes: 
  A) Interactive low-latency (target 95% <150ms, 99% <300ms) — optimize for small payloads and KV cache hits
  B) Settlement batch window (tolerant of slightly higher median latency but needs high throughput sustaining ~2.4k req/s for ~2 mins)

- On streaming: because sessions are sticky we’ll treat each stream as a sustained connection with continuous token throughput. That impacts both concurrent session quotas and cumulative streaming token budget.

Can you ask Priya to attach the CSV and include a breakdown by endpoint, avg tokens/sec per stream, and a 95th pct session duration? That'll let us size baseline connections vs burst capacity.

Suggested timing: Redwood can propose a pilot quota matrix Monday EOD PDT — would that work for FinPay?

Thanks, Marissa

--

Lead, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy

Marissa / team — attaching the traffic export and a short notes column (finpay-traffic-matrix.csv). Highlights from our side: 

- Typical steady-state: ~850 req/s (95th 980 req/s). 
- Peak settlement windows: median 2,100 req/s, 95th 2,430 req/s, 99th 2,800 req/s in extreme months. Windows are usually 60–150s.
- Streams: 4,800 active concurrent user streams at peak; avg tokens/sec per stream 9.6; 95th session duration 1,200s.
- Connections: we expect to open ~500 app-level connections per region. Per-connection multiplexing is limited — most clients keep 1–4 streams per connection.

Notes: we’d like the pilot to test both the interactive mode and one settlement window simulated. Priya attaching CSV to this thread and shared via Drive.

Best,
Priya
Head of Infrastructure, FinPay
priya.shah@finpay.com
[Attachment: finpay-traffic-matrix.csv (CSV)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finpay.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinPay performance alignment & connection strategy

Thanks Priya — this is perfect context. Based on the traffic matrix Redwood proposes the following pilot quota profile (open to adjustments):

- Baseline concurrency (stateless short requests): 350 concurrent request slots (sustained).
- Burst headroom: allow up to 900 concurrent request slots for 3-minute windows (automatic burst tokens), with a soft-deny cutover beyond that; we'll measure error modes during pilot.
- Streaming concurrent sessions: 5,000 concurrent streaming sessions reserved (to match your 4,800 peak margin).
- Streaming token budget: 9.6 tokens/sec * 5,000 sessions * 1.2 factor = 57,600 tokens/sec allowance during peak (we'll meter and report).
- Connection guidance: support 500 TCP connections regionally; recommend connection pool reuse and 1–4 streams per connection.
- Rate limits: per-tenant QPS limit of 3,000 req/s sustained with burst window (as above); per-IP/connection gating to avoid noisy neighbors.
- Pilot credit: Redwood will provision a 4-week pilot with these quotas and a 2000-USD service credit to cover initial tuning (contract Addendum pending).

Open items before we finalize pilot:
1) FinPay to confirm acceptable failure mode if bursts exceed the 3-minute headroom (e.g., queue vs rate-limit rejection).
2) FinPay to confirm whether sticky sessions may be relaxed for a subset (we can simulate both sticky and migratable session models).
3) Schedule a 60m run where FinPay simulates a 2-minute settlement spike and we collect token/latency traces.

If that works we’ll prepare the pilot onboarding checklist and a small playbook for traffic shaping and fallback rules. Proposed kickoff: next Tue 10am PT.

Ben Carter
